brief:
One in eight children in Gaza suffers from stunting, with many showing delayed bone maturation, Al Jazeera English reported. The condition leaves children shorter than their peers and can impair cognitive development. Treatment remains difficult to access amid the ongoing conflict and territorial blockade.

Malnutrition drives the widespread stunting, compounded by limited medical care and disrupted food supplies. Health officials warn the damage may be irreversible if intervention does not come soon, with children facing lifelong physical and developmental consequences from the deprivation.
dek: One in eight children is stunted. Many have bones that have not matured the way they should. Treatment is elusive.
title: War and blockade stunt growth in Gaza's children
